rationale: This program is extremely small (4 functions, ~1 KB of text) and dominated by two hot, loop-heavy functions (main and the sieve routine), so the weight table prioritizes low-cost, high-security transformations and penalizes anything that multiplies loop-body work: SUB gets the highest security/diversity weights since instruction substitution is cheap in both time and space and essentially risk-free on arithmetic-heavy sieve code; IBR is favored next because flattening dispatch via indirect branches obscures control flow with modest overhead suitable for a binary this tiny; BCF and FLA carry high RuntimeCost and SizeCost weights so they are applied selectively only where the feature profile indicates a cold or control-flow-dense region, since bogus paths and loop flattening would disproportionately inflate a 1 KB text section and slow the sieve's inner loops; SPLIT is encouraged as a nearly free diversity booster that helps smaller transforms compose; ICALL is kept moderate with a raised CorrectnessRisk weight because indirect-call rewriting on C++ code with static initializers (_GLOBAL__sub_I_sieve.cpp) can be fragile; and IGV is weighted lowest across the board because this program has minimal global state to protect, making its risk/benefit profile unattractive.
